references.text: The parallel passage in the Sermon on the Mount: "Seek first God's kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well" ([ref:Matt 6:33|Matthew 6:33]). This is the closest parallel to Luke 12:31, with the same exhortation to prioritize God's kingdom over worry about material needs.

The broader context in Matthew's Sermon on the Mount about not worrying about food, drink, and clothing ([ref:Matt 6:25-32|Matthew 6:25-32]) parallels Luke 12:22-30 and forms the background for the promise in verse 31.

The following verse ([ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32]) further explains the promise: "For your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom." God's will is to give the kingdom to his children, which supports the exhortation to seek the kingdom first.

The immediate context ([ref:Luk 12:22-30|Luke 12:22-30]) contains Jesus' teaching about not worrying about life's necessities, because the heavenly Father knows what you need. Verse 31 summarizes this teaching with a positive exhortation.

"Take delight in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart" ([ref:Sal 37:4|Psalms 37:4]). The Old Testament promise that those who seek the Lord and rejoice in him will have their needs met reflects the same principle as in Luke 12:31.

"I was young, and now I am old, yet I have never seen the righteous forsaken or their children begging for bread" ([ref:Sal 37:25|Psalms 37:25]). God's care for the righteous confirms the promise that those who seek his kingdom will receive what they need.

When Solomon asked for wisdom rather than riches, God answered by giving him also what he had not asked for ([ref:1 Kong 3:13-14|1 Kings 3:13-14]). A concrete example of the principle in Luke 12:31: those who seek what belongs to God will also receive earthly things as well.

"The young lions suffer want and hunger, but those who seek the Lord lack nothing" ([ref:Sal 34:10-11|Psalms 34:10-11]). The promise that those who seek the Lord shall not lack anything is an Old Testament parallel to the promise that "all these things" will be given as well.

"He who did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all, how will he not also with him graciously give us all things?" ([ref:Rom 8:32|Romans 8:32]). Paul expresses the same principle: God, who gave the greatest (his Son/the kingdom), will also give the lesser (life's necessities).

"My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus" ([ref:Fil 4:19|Philippians 4:19]). The promise that God meets the needs of his children confirms Jesus' words that those who seek his kingdom will receive what they need as well.
